about: Default app fees for the state layer (D-032: official numbers only; D-042: an estimate is labeled est: true with its observations and direction). A value still null is not yet sourced: the page asks the user for it, and leaves that app out of the comparison until then.

dd.delFee.reason: Not yet sourced (D-042). help.doordash.com/en-us/consumers/article/what-fees-do-i-pay (read 2026-11-17, HTTP 200): "Delivery Fee: A fixed fee per order that varies by merchant", no amount. WSMV (May 21, 2025, https://www.wsmv.com/2025/05/21/nashville-clarksville-we-tested-food-delivery-apps-heres-where-youll-pay-more/) gives four app totals for one McDonald's order and says only that DoorDash's "Delivery fees vary by restaurant and distance"; KIRO 7 (Feb 6, 2025) gives no delivery, small-order or Uber/Grubhub fee amount.

dd.memberMin.quote: a subscription program that offers a $0 delivery fee and reduced service fees for subscribers when ordering $12 or more from any DashPass-eligible restaurant (look for the checkmark). The subscription is $9.99/month
dd.memberMin.reason: Quote sits in the page's Caviar FAQ block but names the DoorDash platform as well. The DashPass terms on the same page give no separate minimum.

dd.memberSvc.quote: The service fee may vary but is 15% of your subtotal for most orders (and 5% for most eligible DashPass restaurant orders).
dd.memberSvc.reason: Stated for markets not yet on the new fee model. Member benefit is a reduced service fee, not a fixed percent cap. Kept as published (D-032); same market caveat as dd.svc.

dd.pickDisc.reason: No standing pickup discount is published ('There are no service fees on pickup orders', help.doordash.com fee page). 0 means no discount; a promo goes in the promo fields. Product rule D-032.

dd.svc.quote: The service fee may vary but is 15% of your subtotal for most orders (and 5% for most eligible DashPass restaurant orders). A flat, minimum service fee may apply.
dd.svc.reason: Figure is from the section for markets NOT yet on the new fee model (California, Chicago, Colorado, DC, Massachusetts, Minnesota, NYC, Puerto Rico, Seattle). Markets on the new model (rolling out late July 2026) price the service fee by distance and order size. Kept as DoorDash's own published figure (D-032, official numbers only); the page and the UI must say it may not match the user's market.

dd.svcMin.quote: DoorDash charges a flat 15% or $3 minimum, so that will work in your favor for orders in the $20 to $100 range.
dd.svcMin.reason: Observations: 1. KIRO 7 (Feb 6, 2025) states the DoorDash service fee once: "a flat 15% or $3 minimum". Median of {3} = 3. No direction choice arises with one observation. The DoorDash fee page (read 2026-11-17) says "a minimum fee may apply" with no amount, so the $3 is secondhand and est: true. Its 15% is DoorDash's own figure (dd.svc), kept as published.

regFee.reason: Not yet sourced (D-042). The only amount is one city: KIRO 7 (Feb 6, 2025) quotes DoorDash's "regulatory response fee of $4.99 on marketplace orders" in Seattle. DoorDash's own fee page (https://help.doordash.com/en-us/consumers/article/what-fees-do-i-pay, read 2026-11-17) says it "may charge this fee when a local or state regulation leads to increased operating costs", that these fees "vary based on region", and that its fee list "currently applies to all U.S. markets except New York City, Seattle, and Puerto Rico". So the Seattle figure comes from a market outside DoorDash's general fee list, and isn't an observation of the typical place. Null until observations from places in the general list exist (the user's checkouts, ISS-034).
